QF.id: XIII Introduction to the Underlying Markets_41

question.text: If USDJPY is quoted at 115.08/115.09 and USDINR at 75.64/75.65, what is the offer rate for JPYINR (price of 100 JPY in INR)?

answer.text: 65.73 (calculated as 75.65/115.09 × 100, using the wrong USDJPY side)
65.76 (calculated as 75.66/115.08 × 100, using an incorrect USDINR offer)

explanation.text: The Logic: To buy 100 JPY using INR (offer side of JPYINR), buy USD with INR at the USDINR offer of 75.65 and then sell USD for JPY at the USDJPY bid of 115.08 (the bank buys USD at its bid). The JPYINR offer therefore equals (75.65 / 115.08) × 100 = 65.74 (rounded from 65.7369). The Trap: The common error is using the USDJPY offer (115.09) instead of the bid, or using the wrong USDINR side. Both inputs must reflect the direction of the trade through the USD leg. Note: When USD is the base in both pairs (USDINR and USDJPY), the JPYINR cross is obtained by division, not multiplication, and the correct bid/offer combination depends on which side of each underlying pair is hit.
